Freon-12, also known as chlorofluorocarbon-12 (CFC-12), is a refrigerant gas that was widely used in air conditioning and refrigeration systems. However, due to its contribution to ozone depletion, the Montreal Protocol, an international treaty signed in 1987, phased out the production and use of CFC-12 by the year 2000. The treaty aimed to reduce the production of CFC-12 by 50% by the end of the century, with developed countries stopping production by 1996 and developing countries by 2006. The phase-out of CFC-12 has led to the development of alternative refrigerants, such as R-134a, which is being used in new air-conditioning systems. However, converting older systems to use R-134a can be costly, ranging from $200 to $800, depending on the complexity of the conversion.
